content.introduction: Pagrin derives a whole identity package from a single approved mark. Nothing downstream holds a copy, so nothing downstream can go out of date.
content.markRationale: A fan of rays springing from a single point at the lower left, widening as they go, cut off square by the edge of the tile. It is one closed path rather than a set of separate shapes, and it takes its colour from a single linear gradient laid across the whole of it, so the mark carries the spectrum as one thing and has no flat colour in it anywhere. That is also why it wants room: the rays taper to a hairline where they meet, and below the floor stated here they close up into a solid block.
content.colourRationale: Signal carries the product and the page. Ember is the warm end of the mark's own gradient and marks the single most important thing on a screen, never more than five percent of it. Ink and Page do the reading.
content.typeRationale: The interface is set in the system stack, so the package specifies Schibsted Grotesk, the nearest grotesque it can ship, and inlines it. The wordmark is drawn in Helvetica Neue Bold and delivered as outlines, so it needs no font at all.

misuse.why: The rays converge at the lower left. Turned, they point nowhere.
Use a named colourway. The gradient is one of them.
Use a flat colourway over a photograph, never the gradient.
